items.abstract_or_text: # Release v5.21.0 ## New Model additions ### MiniCPM-OCR MiniCPM-OCR is a document-understanding model from OpenBMB's MiniCPM-V family. It keeps the MiniCPM-V 4.6 architecture, which pairs a SigLIP vision encoder and a window-attention merger with a Qwen3.5 language model. It is specialized for reading text-dense images such as scanned pages, screenshots, receipts and tables. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/minicpm_ocr) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.18154) * Feat test (#49920) by @guarin in [#49920](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49920) ### Flint Flint is Recursive's mixture-of-experts language model. Compared to a standard SwiGLU MoE transformer such as Qwen3-MoE, it uses hybrid attention (sliding-window attention with rotary embeddings over the current token and the previous 512 tokens in most layers, and full attention without positional encoding in the remaining layers). It also has learned attention sinks, as in GPT-OSS, with per-head RMS-normalized queries and keys. Each sparse layer routes a token to 6 of 256 experts by sigmoid score and adds an ungated shared expert, and the first two layers are dense. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/flint) * Add Flint model support. (#49824) by @lovishmadaan in [#49824](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49824) ### UltraVBert UltraVBert extends ModernVBert by pairing the UltraBERT text encoder with a SigLIP vision encoder for visual document understanding and retrieval. Its image processor splits each page into 512-pixel tiles plus a global view. The connector merges each 4 x 4 block of vision patches into one token, so a tile becomes 64 image tokens, and RMS-normalizes them to the scale of UltraBERT's token embeddings. The `max_image_tiles` setting (27 by default) caps the number of tiles per page. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/ultravbert) * Add UltraVBERT (#49685) by @athrael-soju in [#49685](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49685) ### Gradium Phonon TTS Gradium Phonon TTS is Gradium's family of on-device text-to-speech models, trained with the Pocket TTS recipe. A causal transformer reads a voice prompt and the text, then emits one continuous 32-dimensional audio latent per step at 12.5 Hz through a one-step flow head, and an end-of-speech head decides when the utterance ends. The latents are decoded to 24 kHz audio by a Pocket TTS audio tokenizer. Unlike Pocket TTS, voice conditioning uses 512-dimensional latents from a separate, unreleased speaker codec, so voices come as precomputed latents and cannot be cloned from a recording. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/gradium_phonon_tts) * Add GradiumPhononTTS (#49791) by @eustlb in [#49791](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49791) ### Pocket TTS Pocket TTS is Kyutai's 100M-parameter text-to-speech model, built as a Continuous Audio Language Model that runs faster than real time on CPU. A causal transformer emits one continuous audio latent per frame (12.5 Hz) through a one-step flow head, and an end-of-speech head decides when to stop. A Mimi-based audio tokenizer encodes voice prompts and decodes the generated latents to 24 kHz audio. Two flow heads are released, Lagrangian self-distillation (default) and drifting, and voices can be cloned from a recording, passed as precomputed latents, or loaded from cached KV states. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/pocket_tts) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.06926 (the Continuous Audio Language Models paper, arXiv 2509.06926). It is the only paper the documentation links, and it describes the architecture family Pocket TTS belongs to. The docs do not cite a separate Pocket TTS technical report.) | [Blog Post](NONE. The documentation links no official blog post. It points only to the original code repository at https://github.com/kyutai-labs/pocket-tts.) * add PocketTTS (#49589) by @eustlb in [#49589](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49589) ### Pocket TTS Audio Tokenizer The Pocket TTS audio tokenizer is the codec used by Pocket TTS. It has Mimi's architecture (SEANet convolutions plus a small causal transformer on each side), but its residual vector quantizer is replaced by a continuous 32-dimensional bottleneck, the VAE-GAN from Continuous Audio Language Models. It converts 24 kHz audio into latents at 12.5 Hz and decodes them back to audio. It serves as the `audio_tokenizer` of `PocketTTSProcessor`, encoding voice prompts and decoding generated latents, and its encoder and decoder can also be loaded on their own. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/pocket_tts_audio_tokenizer) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.06926 (Continuous Audio Language Models, whose VAE-GAN this tokenizer uses; arxiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.06926)) * add PocketTTSAudioTokenizer (#49588) by @eustlb in [#49588](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49588) ## Breaking changes Fixed Gemma4 processor imports (the Gemma4, Gemma4 unified and EmbeddingGemma2 processors) so `from transformers import *` no longer fails in environments that have `PIL` but not `torch`; no user action is needed. * :rotating_light: Fix gemma4 cross imports resulting in import failing without `torch` but with `PIL` (#49748) by @Sai-Suraj-27 Added an `"fp8"` backend to `QuantizedCache`, alongside `quanto` and `hqq`, that stores KV states in `torch.float8_e4m3fn` with a single scale per tensor; enable it with `cache_implementation="quantized"` and `cache_config={"backend": "fp8"}`. * 🚨Add an FP8 backend to `QuantizedCache` (#48677) by @jiqing-feng Tensor parallelism now has a dedicated embedding style, shards every model's input embeddings by default, and supports widths that aren't divisible by the TP size, so `ColwiseParallel` and `RowwiseParallel` now apply only to linear layers; custom TP plans that applied them to embeddings must switch to the new embedding style. * 🚨 TP: give embeddings their own style, shard input embeddings by default, and shard widths that don't divide by the TP size (#49570) by @IlyasMoutawwakil Every MoE TP and EP plan now shards its experts, so models no longer keep all experts on every rank, and a new `test_moe_parallel_plans_shard_experts` test enforces this; custom or downstream MoE parallel plans must add expert sharding to pass it and to avoid wasted memory. * 🚨 MoE: shard the experts in every TP/EP plan, and test for it (#49206) by @IlyasMoutawwakil ## Cache This release improves cache handling across the library. Flash Attention now works with static caches, BLOOM no longer crashes with static cache or compiled generate, chunked prefill supports cache continuation, and the Qwen4-Exp indexer's position history stays aligned with its cached keys. Linear-attention caches also gain new getters (`is_recording_past`, `get_recurrent_state`, conv-state access) that stop exposing cache internals and prepare for paged-c * [FA] Fix FA with static cache (#49998) by @Cyrilvallez in [#49998] * [docs] CB cache behavior (#49025) by @stevhliu in [#49025] * [CB] Reduce warmup time by not computing attention over full cache (#49853) by @remi-or in [#49853] * Fix Qwen4-Exp indexer position cache lifecycle (#49840) by @taking-lying-flat in [#49840] * [Cache] Linear attn cache: use new getters (#49375) by @remi-or in [#49375] * [Cache] Get conv states (#49309) by @remi-or in [#49309] * [Cache] Add get_recurrent_state (#49306) by @remi-or in [#49306] * [Cache] Add is_recording_past (#49305) by @remi-or in [#49305] * Fix BLOOM crash with static cache / compiled generate (#49481) by @kaixuanliu in [#49481] * Allow Cache continuation for chunked prefill (#49662) by @Cyrilvallez in [#49662] ## Vision Vision image processors now composite PNG transparency onto white instead of exposing black pixels, and `background_color` is preserved correctly across the DeepSeek-VL and Janus processors. items.abstract_or_text: ggml-cpu : rewrite concat as one row kernel for all types (#31179) Every dst row comes from src0 or src1, or for dim 0 from the row of src0 followed by the row of src1, so a single kernel covers every type: a dense source row is one memcpy, quantized types included, and a strided source is copied element by element with the element size known at compile time. Rows are split across threads instead of i2 alone, which is often 1, and are copied in tiles of 32: for a transposed source the elements are walked in the outer loop, so the rows of a tile read neighboring addresses instead of jumping a full row stride per element. Add transposed b cases to test_concat, the layout of the delta-net conv input, and a perf case for it. **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - [macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b11906/llama-b11906-bin-macos-arm64.tar.gz) - items.abstract_or_text: common, grammar: add recursive depth limit, make it a requirement (#31153) * common, grammar: add recursive depth limit, make it a requirement * catch more recursive functions * common : tidy up peg parser changes * grammar : reject candidates in a loop, without a depth limit The depth limit in llama_grammar_reject_candidates_for_stack counted the code points of a vocab token, so any token of 256 chars or more was always rejected under a grammar, such as the 512-space token of GLM-4.7-Flash or the long space tokens of Laguna-S-2.1. The rejection now walks the code points with its own stack of levels instead of recursing: there is no limit and no stack risk, whatever the length of a token from the GGUF, and the masks match master. * grammar : track rejected candidates as indices into the input At a given code point a candidate only differs from its input by the position of its code point pointer, so the levels now carry indices into the input candidates instead of copies. The first level needs no special case and the rejects map back to the input directly. Grammar sampling gets faster than master on GLM-4.7, Laguna, Qwen3.6 and gemma-4 with the json, list and spaces grammars, same masks. * nit : shorten the comment of llama_grammar_reject_step * common : add depth_guard for schema walks * grammar : move GRAMMAR_RECURSIVE_LIMIT into the .cpp * common : reduce recursion limit for peg parser * improve --------- Co-authored-by: Alde Rojas Co-authored-by: Pascal **Website:** - items.abstract_or_text: llama-quant : fix 4D tensor quantization using ggml_nrows() and name-based expert detection (#30820) * llama-quant : fix quantizing 4D tensors nrows_total was ne[1]*ne[2], so for a 4D tensor only the first ne[2] slices were quantized and the rest of the rows were dropped. Use ggml_nrows(tensor) to count all rows, including ne[3]. Fixes #29916 * llama-quant : detect expert tensors by name and fix imatrix size for 4D tensors The MXFP4_MOE path used ne[2] > 1 to detect MoE expert tensors. This is wrong for non-expert tensors with 3 or more dims, e.g. MLA projections (BailingMoE3) and 4D conv kernels. Use the tensor name instead: all tensors used by GGML_OP_MUL_MAT_ID are named *_exps or *_chexps. This also removes the BailingMoE3 special case. The imatrix holds one vector of ne[0] values per 2D slice, so the expected size is ne[0]*ne[2]*ne[3], not ne[0]*ne[2]. This matches how the imatrix is indexed per row for 4D tensors in llama_tensor_quantize_impl. items.abstract_or_text: CUDA: fuse FFN gate/up matmuls and GLU in MMQ with interleaved gate/up rows (#29948) * cuda: fuse FFN gate/up and GLU in MMQ with interleaved gate/up rows For prompt processing, run the gate and up matmuls of a dense FFN as one mul_mat_q launch and apply the GLU in the write-back. - The loaders take the gate weights as a second pointer and fill the weight tile with up and gate rows interleaved in chunks of 8, so each thread holds an up value and the matching gate value (rows r and r + 8 of an MMA tile). - The MMA loop is unchanged: same tile, warp layout, vec_dot and one sum[] per thread. The fused write-back computes the GLU from registers and writes half the rows. - The fused path uses the regular tiling (no stream-k) with the column tiles innermost so that neighbouring blocks share weight tiles. - Enabled for Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, Q8_0 and IQ4_XS on NVIDIA Turing and newer. * cuda: assert the fused MMQ gate argument and trim redundant comments * cuda: move the fused MMQ hint check to should_fuse and add TODOs * cuda: pass prec_src1 to the fused MMQ write-back * cuda: fuse only with efficient tiling and no fallback, merge the GLU write-back * cuda: require has_fusion explicitly, drop the fusion-only src1 precision check * cuda: launch the fused MMQ kernel through the stream-k kernel with one block per tile * cuda: inline the MMQ tiling-efficiency check * tests: one fused gate/up MMQ case per type and GLU op * cuda: always launch the fused MMQ kernel with one block per tile * tests: shorten the fused gate/up MMQ test comment * cuda: select the fused MMQ loader and write-back in ggml_cuda_mmq_get_util_funcs * cuda: run the fused MMQ kernel on the plain tiling path * cuda: put the column tiles innermost in the MMQ plain tiling path **Website:** - items.abstract_or_text: vulkan : one warp tile per subgroup in the small matmul tiles (#30106) WM of the small tiles was 32, or 8 for 8-wide subgroups, whatever the tile's BLOCK_SIZE and WARP. With 16-wide subgroups (Mali) the second subgroup of a workgroup wrote into the next tile's columns. With 8-wide subgroups some _id tiles left rows uncomputed.
